target: Buenas noches.
english: Good evening / Good night.

target: De nada.
english: You're welcome.

target: ¿Habla inglés?
english: Do you speak English?

target: ¿Cuánto cuesta?
english: How much does it cost?

target: ¿Sabes cocinar paella?
english: Do you know how to cook paella?
grammar: Saber: 2nd person = sabes. Saber + infinitive = to know how to.

target: Se me hace tarde.
english: I'm running late.
grammar: 'Hacerse' in impersonal expressions: 'se me hace tarde' = it's getting late for me. The indirect object pronoun shows who is affected.

target: Escribo un correo electrónico.
english: I write an email.

target: El bebé tiene hambre.
english: The baby is hungry.

target: Me hace ilusión verte.
english: I'm excited to see you.

target: Creo que tienes razón.
english: I think you are right.
grammar: Many common Spanish verbs are irregular in the 'yo' form – memorize these first as they're the most frequent.

target: Vamos para el aeropuerto.
english: We're heading to the airport.
grammar: para = destination / purpose (for him, in order TO eat). por = reason / exchange (because of him, for ten euros). Ask "why?" → por, "what for?" → para.

target: ¿Puede llamar un taxi?
english: Can you call a taxi?

target: Mi hermana trabaja en un hospital.
english: My sister works in a hospital.
grammar: 'Trabajar en' = to work at/in a place. 'En' before an indefinite article: 'en un hospital' = at a hospital.

target: Me alegra saber que estás bien.
english: I'm glad to know you're well.

target: Estoy bien, gracias.
english: I am fine, thanks.
grammar: Estar for temporary states: how you feel right now.

target: ¿Tiene usted reserva?
english: Do you have a reservation?
grammar: Usted – formal you, used in service contexts and with strangers.

target: La cena está lista.
english: Dinner is ready.
grammar: Estar for temporary states/results: la cena está lista (it's ready now).

target: Extraño a mi familia.
english: I miss my family.

target: Creo que tengo fiebre.
english: I think I have a fever.

target: ¿Tiene disponibilidad para mañana?
english: Do you have availability for tomorrow?

target: ¿Dónde está la oficina del jefe?
english: Where is the boss's office?

target: Yo pienso mucho antes de decidir.
english: I think a lot before I decide.
grammar: "Pensar" has a e→ie stem change: the "e" in the stem becomes "ie" when stressed (all singular + 3rd plural). Nosotros/vosotros keep the original stem.

target: ¿Cuántos años tienes?
english: How old are you?
grammar: Age uses "tener" (to have), not "ser" (to be). Literally: "How many years do you have?" Tengo 25 años = I am 25 years old.

target: ¿Qué quieres hacer?
english: What do you want to do?
grammar: "Querer" (to want) + infinitive: quiero comer (I want to eat), quieres hacer (you want to do). Querer is stem-changing: e→ie.

target: ¿El desayuno está incluido?
english: Is breakfast included?

target: Estoy un poco cansado.
english: I'm a little tired.
grammar: Adjectives agree with the subject: cansado (m), cansada (f). A woman would say "estoy cansada." Estar is used because tiredness is temporary.

target: Mi prima está embarazada.
english: My cousin is pregnant.
grammar: Estar for states/conditions: está embarazada. Never use ser here.

target: El vuelo es directo.
english: The flight is direct.
grammar: "Ser" is used for inherent characteristics. The flight IS direct – it's a defining feature of this flight.

target: Estoy aquí por una reunión.
english: I'm here for a meeting.
grammar: Por for reason / cause.

target: Hoy es un buen día.
english: Today is a good day.
grammar: "Bueno" shortens to "buen" before a masculine singular noun. Similarly: malo → mal, primero → primer, tercero → tercer.

target: ¿De dónde eres tú?
english: Where are you from?

target: Ella es mi amiga.
english: She is my friend.
grammar: Gender agreement: amigo (male friend) → amiga (female friend). Most nouns ending in -o are masculine, -a are feminine.

target: Esto es un libro.
english: This is a book.
grammar: "Un" is the indefinite article for masculine nouns (a/an). Un libro (a book), una mesa (a table). "El/la" are the definite articles (the).

target: Buenos días, ¿cómo estás?
english: Good morning, how are you?
grammar: Use `estar` when the answer could change tomorrow: location, feelings, ongoing actions. `estar + adjective` = it's a state, not a label.

target: No llegues tarde otra vez.
english: Don't be late again.
grammar: 'Otro/a' never takes an indefinite article: 'otro día' (another day), never 'un otro día.'

target: ¿Prefieres la ciudad o el campo?
english: Do you prefer the city or the countryside?

target: Me duele la cabeza.
english: My head hurts.
grammar: 'Doler' works like 'gustar': the body part is the subject. 'Me duele la cabeza' = My head hurts (lit. the head hurts to me). Plural: 'me duelen los pies.'

target: Me duele la espalda.
english: My back hurts.
grammar: "Doler" uses the gustar pattern: the thing causing the feeling is the subject. "Me doler..." = "... is [feeling] to me." Use singular for one thing, plural for multiple.

target: La radio no funciona.
english: The radio doesn't work.
grammar: "La radio" – feminine because it's short for "la radioemisora." Gender follows the full word.

target: Me hacen gracia sus chistes.
english: His jokes make me laugh.
grammar: "Hacer gracia" uses the gustar pattern: the thing causing the feeling is the subject. "Me hacer..." = "... is [feeling] to me." Use singular for one thing, plural for multiple.

target: La empresa es grande.
english: The company is big.
grammar: Size adjectives typically follow the noun: 'una casa grande,' 'un perro pequeño.'

target: Hace buen tiempo hoy.
english: The weather is nice today.
grammar: "Hacer" is used for weather: "hace calor" (it's hot), "hace frío" (it's cold).

target: Mi padre es muy alto.
english: My father is very tall.

target: Tenemos comida para tres días.
english: We have food for three days.

target: No hay problema.
english: No problem.
grammar: "Hay" means "there is" or "there are" – it's the same for singular and plural. Hay un gato. Hay tres gatos.

target: Voy por agua.
english: I'm going for water.
grammar: "Por" = to get/fetch: "Fui por pan." Going somewhere to pick something up.

target: Es importante llegar a tiempo.
english: It's important to arrive on time.

target: Ella está embarazada.
english: She's pregnant.
grammar: Estar for conditions: "Está roto." Use estar for the current state/condition of something.

target: Ella es soltera.
english: She's single.
grammar: Ser for civil status: "Es casada." Marital status uses ser – it defines identity, not a passing state.

target: Te quiero mucho.
english: I love you very much.

target: Estudio en la universidad.
english: I study at the university.
grammar: 'Estudiar' is regular -ar. 'En' before institutions means 'at': 'estudio en la universidad' = I study at the university.

target: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas aquí?
english: How long have you been here?
grammar: "Llevar" + time = to have been (doing something) for (duration). Llevo dos años aquí = I've been here for two years. Very common construction.

target: ¿Cómo llego al museo?
english: How do I get to the museum?
grammar: "Llego" from "llegar" (to arrive). "¿Cómo llego a...?" is the standard way to ask for directions.

target: ¿Cómo se llama tu sobrina?
english: What is your niece's name?
grammar: '¿Cómo?' means 'how?' with accent. Without accent, 'como' means 'like/as' or 'I eat.'

target: El día está nublado.
english: The sky is cloudy.
grammar: "El día" is masculine – an exception. "Buenos días" (good days) shows the masculine adjective form.

target: El poema es precioso.
english: The poem is beautiful.
grammar: "El poema" is masculine. Greek-origin -ma words: poema, tema, problema, sistema – all masculine.

target: Me encantó la comida local.
english: I loved the local food.
grammar: "Encantar" works like "gustar": the thing loved is the subject. "Me encantó" = it enchanted me.

target: Ellos vuelven del viaje el lunes.
english: They come back from the trip on Monday.
grammar: "Volver" has a o→ue stem change: the "o" in the stem becomes "ue" when stressed (all singular + 3rd plural). Nosotros/vosotros keep the original stem.

target: El proyecto es interesante.
english: The project is interesting.

target: Hoy hay mucho tráfico.
english: There's a lot of traffic today.
grammar: Don't confuse `hay` (there is) with `ahí` (over there) or `ay` (ouch). `Hay` is the impersonal form of `haber` and never gets a subject.

target: Me gusta mucho esta ciudad.
english: I really like this city.
grammar: "Gustar" works backwards from English: the thing you like is the subject. "Me gusta la ciudad" = the city pleases me. "Me gustan los gatos" = cats please me (plural).

target: Mi madre es muy cariñosa.
english: My mother is very caring.

target: La reunión es importante.
english: The meeting is important.
grammar: Ser for characteristics: traits that define what something IS use ser, not estar.

target: Mi carro es azul.
english: My car is blue.
grammar: Ser for inherent color: "El cielo es azul." Use ser for colors seen as defining traits.

target: La plaza está llena de gente.
english: The square is full of people.
grammar: "Estar" for temporary states. The square is full now, but it won't always be.

target: Ella es alta pero está cansada.
english: She is tall but she's tired.

target: Estamos a veinte de marzo.
english: It is March twentieth.

target: La cena costó cuarenta euros.
english: Dinner cost forty euros.

target: Compré los billetes por internet.
english: I bought the tickets online.
grammar: "Por internet" – "por" indicates the means/medium through which something is done.

target: Vivimos en un departamento pequeño.
english: We live in a small apartment.
grammar: Piso = apartment (Spain). In Latin America: departamento or apartamento.

target: La foto salió borrosa.
english: The photo came out blurry.
grammar: "La foto" – feminine because it's short for "la fotografía." Shortened words keep the gender of the full word.

target: ¿Cuánto tiempo trabajaste allí?
english: How long did you work there?

target: Te llamo por teléfono.
english: I'll call you by phone.
grammar: "Por" = via: "Lo dije por teléfono." Por for the method of communication.

target: Quiero visitar la catedral.
english: I want to visit the cathedral.

target: Ayer llovió todo el día.
english: Yesterday it rained all day.

target: Se nos acabó la leche.
english: We ran out of milk.
grammar: "Se nos acabó" – "se" construction for unplanned events.

target: Ellos decidieron cancelar la reunión.
english: They decided to cancel the meeting.

target: Ellos se mudaron a otra ciudad.
english: They moved to another city.

target: Él trajo flores para su madre.
english: He brought flowers for his mother.

target: Mi abuela cocinaba los mejores postres.
english: My grandmother used to cook the best desserts.

target: Lo hizo a propósito para molestarme.
english: He did it on purpose to annoy me.

target: Me equivoqué de dirección y me perdí.
english: I got the address wrong and got lost.

target: Se rompió mi computadora en la peor semana.
english: My computer broke during the worst week.

target: Él se puso contento al oír la noticia.
english: He became happy when he heard the news.

target: ¿Por qué no viniste?
english: Why didn't you come?
grammar: "¿Por qué?" (two words, with accent) = Why? "Porque" (one word, no accent) = Because. The accent and spacing matter.

target: Ayer hice tres entrevistas.
english: Yesterday I did three interviews.
grammar: "Hacer" has an irregular preterite stem (hice...). These irregular preterites share the same endings: -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. No accents needed.

target: La entrevista fue muy bien.
english: The interview went very well.

target: Una copa de vino tinto.
english: A glass of red wine.

target: Mientras llovía, llegamos al hotel.
english: While it was raining, we arrived at the hotel.

target: De pequeño quería ser astronauta.
english: As a kid, I wanted to be an astronaut.

target: Ella se fue sin decir adiós.
english: She left without saying goodbye.

target: El tren que tomamos fue puntual.
english: The train we took was on time.

target: Mi abuelo pescaba en el río.
english: My grandfather fished in the river.

target: Me puse nerviosa antes de la presentación.
english: I got nervous before the presentation.

target: Tu presentación fue mejor que la mía.
english: Your presentation was better than mine.

target: Desde mi punto de vista, la negociación fue un éxito.
english: From my point of view, the negotiation was a success.

target: Te lo dije ayer.
english: I told you yesterday.
grammar: Double object pronouns: te (you) + lo (it).

target: Se lo dije ayer.
english: I told him yesterday.
grammar: Double object pronouns: indirect (le/les) + direct (lo/la) → "se lo." Le becomes se before lo/la to avoid "le lo." "Se lo dije" = I told it to him.

target: Yo siempre olvido las contraseñas.
english: I always forget passwords.

target: Antes trabajaba en una fábrica.
english: I used to work in a factory.

target: De pequeño odiaba las verduras.
english: As a kid, I hated vegetables.

target: Mi antiguo jefe era muy estricto.
english: My former boss was very strict.

target: Me quedé dormido en el autobús.
english: I fell asleep on the bus.

target: Mientras cocino suelo escuchar un pódcast.
english: While I cook I usually listen to a podcast.

target: Mientras cruzábamos la frontera, llovía mucho.
english: While we crossed the border, it rained a lot.

target: El restaurante donde cenamos estaba muy lleno.
english: The restaurant where we had dinner was very crowded.

target: El barrio donde nos perdimos era muy pintoresco.
english: The neighborhood where we got lost was very picturesque.

target: Me siento frustrado porque nada sale como quiero.
english: I feel frustrated because nothing goes the way I want.

target: Ellos se ayudan mutuamente.
english: They help each other.

target: Gracias por tu ayuda.
english: Thanks for your help.
grammar: "Por" = because of: "Llegué tarde por el tráfico." Expresses the cause behind something.

target: Hace mucho viento hoy.
english: It is very windy today.

target: Lo cambié por otro.
english: I exchanged it for another.
grammar: "Por" = in exchange for: "Lo compré por diez euros." Por marks what you give to get something.

target: Ella trabajaba mientras estudiaba.
english: She worked while she studied.

target: Cuando llegues al hotel, avísame.
english: When you arrive at the hotel, let me know.
grammar: "Cuando" + future action uses subjunctive: "cuando llegues" (not "cuando llegas").

target: Es importante que bebas suficiente agua.
english: It's important that you drink enough water.

target: Sin que nadie se dé cuenta, salimos.
english: Without anyone noticing, we left.

target: Mi primo se rompió el brazo jugando.
english: My cousin broke his arm playing.

target: Mi madre me aconseja que ahorre más.
english: My mother advises me to save more.

target: Nos reunimos cada lunes.
english: We meet every Monday.

target: Nos echamos de menos.
english: We miss each other.
grammar: "Echarse de menos" = to miss each other. "Nos echamos de menos" = We miss each other.

target: Te lo explico ahora.
english: I'll explain it to you now.
grammar: Double pronouns: indirect + direct. "Te lo dije" = I told it to you. Indirect pronoun (te) goes first, then direct (lo).

target: Se me olvidó enviar el correo.
english: I forgot to send the email.
grammar: Se me olvidó: accidental se construction – 'it slipped my mind'.

target: Me bajé en la parada equivocada.
english: I got off at the wrong stop.

target: Me alegra que hayamos llegado a tiempo.
english: I'm glad we arrived on time.

target: Se me olvidó recoger a los niños.
english: I forgot to pick up the kids.
grammar: Se me olvidó = it slipped my mind (accidental se construction).

target: La receta necesita trescientos gramos de harina.
english: The recipe needs three hundred grams of flour.

target: Para ser honesto, no me gustó el hotel.
english: To be honest, I didn't like the hotel.

target: Es importante tener un fondo de emergencia para gastos imprevistos.
english: It's important to have an emergency fund for unexpected expenses.

target: Hago ejercicio por salud.
english: I exercise for health.

target: Te lo devuelvo mañana.
english: I'll return it to you tomorrow.
grammar: Double object pronouns: "te lo" – to you + it.

target: Le cuesta levantarse temprano.
english: He has a hard time getting up early.

target: Creo que es por aquí.
english: I think it's this way.

target: Este regalo es para ti.
english: This gift is for you.
grammar: "Para" = for (recipient): "Es para ti." Para marks who receives something.

target: Mi hermano toca la guitarra.
english: My brother plays the guitar.

target: Me sorprende que no lo sepas.
english: I'm surprised you don't know.

target: No puedo ir por el trabajo.
english: I can't go because of work.
grammar: "Por" = because of. Expresses the cause or obstacle: "No salimos por la lluvia" (We didn't go out because of the rain).

target: Me iría de vacaciones ahora mismo.
english: I'd go on vacation right now.

target: Debería habérselo dicho antes en lugar de esperar.
english: You should have told them sooner instead of waiting.

target: Me gusta la música.
english: I like music.
grammar: "Me" is indirect object – music pleases me.

target: Lo solucioné yo solo.
english: I solved it by myself.

target: ¿Les mandaste el correo?
english: Did you send them the email?
grammar: "Les" = to them (indirect object): "Les dije la verdad" = I told them the truth. Plural of le.

target: La primavera empieza en marzo.
english: Spring starts in March.

target: La ciudad tiene mucha historia.
english: The city has a lot of history.

target: Se lo prometí a mi hijo.
english: I promised it to my son.

target: Espero que tengas un buen día.
english: I hope you have a good day.

target: Le di mi opinión al director.
english: I gave my opinion to the director.

target: Ojalá consigamos entradas para el parque.
english: I hope we get tickets to the park.

target: Me perdí en las callejuelas del centro.
english: I got lost in the narrow streets of the center.

target: El suelo de la cocina es de baldosas blancas.
english: The kitchen floor is made of white tiles.

target: ¿Me pasas la sal y la pimienta, por favor?
english: Can you pass me the salt and pepper, please?

target: La moto está aparcada fuera.
english: The motorcycle is parked outside.
grammar: "La moto" – feminine because it's short for "la motocicleta." Keeps gender of the full word.

target: Espero que llegues a tiempo.
english: I hope you arrive on time.
grammar: Espero que + subjunctive: hoping about someone else's action triggers subjunctive. "Espero que vengas" (I hope you come).

target: No hay ningún taxi que pueda llevarme ahora.
english: There's no taxi that can take me now.
grammar: hay = there is / there are. Doesn't change for plural: hay un libro and hay tres libros. Different verb from tener (to have).

target: A menos que llueva, vamos a la playa.
english: Unless it rains, we're going to the beach.
grammar: A menos que always takes subjunctive.

target: Creo que es importante que hablemos de esto.
english: I think it's important that we talk about this.

target: Aun cuando no estemos de acuerdo, nos respetamos.
english: Even when we don't agree, we respect each other.

target: Lo que pasó ayer no puede volver a pasar.
english: What happened yesterday cannot happen again.

target: Haga lo que haga, siempre encuentra algo que criticar.
english: Whatever he does, he always finds something to criticize.
grammar: "Haga lo que haga" = whatever I do. Subjunctive repeated: verb + lo que + same verb. Universal concession pattern.

target: Ponme una caña y una ración de croquetas de jamón.
english: Give me a small beer and a portion of ham croquettes.

target: La directora anuncio que habria cambios importantes en la empresa.
english: The director announced there would be important changes in the company.

target: En caso de que el bebé se despierte, dale el biberón.
english: In case the baby wakes up, give him the bottle.
grammar: En caso de que + subjunctive = in case.

target: Puse las flores en un jarrón en la mesa del salón.
english: I put the flowers in a vase on the living room table.

target: El edificio no tiene ascensor y vivimos en el quinto piso.
english: The building has no elevator and we live on the fifth floor.

target: El turismo rural es una forma estupenda de conocer la cultura local.
english: Rural tourism is a wonderful way to get to know the local culture.

target: Ten cuidado con el escalón.
english: Be careful with the step.
grammar: Irregular tú command: "Ten" (have/hold). One of eight irregular tú commands: haz, di, sal, ven, ten, pon, sé, ve.

target: Di la verdad, ¿fuiste tú?
english: Tell the truth, was it you?
grammar: "Di" = Say/Tell (command). Irregular tú command of decir. "Dime la verdad" = Tell me the truth.

target: Me da pena que se vaya.
english: It makes me sad that she's leaving.

target: Si termino pronto, ayudaré con tu parte.
english: If I finish early, I'll help with your part.

target: El guía nos explicó la historia del monumento.
english: The guide explained the monument's history to us.

target: Habría que tener en cuenta la diferencia horaria.
english: One should take the time difference into account.

target: Dile que venga a la reunión a las cuatro.
english: Tell him to come to the meeting at four.

target: Me desperté a medianoche porque oí un ruido fuerte.
english: I woke up at midnight because I heard a loud noise.

target: Los colegas con quienes almuerzo son de otro departamento.
english: The colleagues I have lunch with are from another department.
grammar: "Con quienes" = with whom (plural): preposition + quienes for people in formal relative clauses.

target: Si no fuera por mi familia, no habría seguido adelante.
english: If it weren't for my family, I wouldn't have kept going.

target: ¿Le importaría esperar un momento?
english: Would you mind waiting a moment?
grammar: "¿Le importaría...?" = Would you mind...? Very formal polite request using conditional of importar.

target: Quería que supieras la verdad.
english: I wanted you to know the truth.
grammar: Quería que + imperfect subjunctive: "Quería que lo supieras" (I wanted you to know). Past main clause + que → imperfect subjunctive.

target: Me encantaría volver a este lugar algún día.
english: I'd love to come back to this place someday.

target: Nos aconsejaron que no bebiéramos agua del grifo.
english: They advised us not to drink tap water.

target: ¿Le importaría indicarme cómo llegar a la plaza mayor?
english: Would you mind telling me how to get to the main square?

target: El equipo con el que trabajo es muy profesional.
english: The team I work with is very professional.

target: El norte de España es más verde que el sur.
english: The north of Spain is greener than the south.

target: La isla a la que queremos ir está muy lejos.
english: The island we want to go to is very far.

target: De tal palo, tal astilla; el hijo es identico al padre.
english: Like father, like son – the son is identical to the father.
grammar: De tal palo, tal astilla = the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

target: Prefiero ir en carro compartido porque es más barato y más sostenible.
english: I prefer ride-sharing because it's cheaper and more sustainable.

target: No sé qué habrá pasado.
english: I don't know what could have happened.
grammar: Future perfect for past speculation: "¿Qué habrá pasado?" (What could have happened?). Guessing about past events.

target: ¿A qué hora volveremos al hotel?
english: What time will we return to the hotel?
grammar: '¿A qué hora...?' = At what time...? The preposition 'a' is required with clock times.

target: Lo que me preocupa es que no tenemos suficiente tiempo.
english: What worries me is that we don't have enough time.

target: La razón por la que llegué tarde fue el tráfico.
english: The reason I arrived late was the traffic.
grammar: "Por la que" = for which: "La razón por la que vine" = The reason for which I came.

target: Si hubiera aprendido inglés de pequeño, ahora lo hablaría perfectamente.
english: If I had learned English as a child, I would speak it perfectly now.

target: Mi compañera de trabajo se ha convertido en una buena amiga.
english: My coworker has become a good friend.

target: El comercio electrónico ha cambiado la forma en que compramos casi todo.
english: E-commerce has changed the way we buy almost everything.

target: Hice una copia de seguridad de todos mis archivos en la nube.
english: I made a backup of all my files in the cloud.

target: Esta semana he cambiado mi rutina para hacer ejercicio por la mañana.
english: This week I've changed my routine to exercise in the morning.

target: Necesito una tabla de cortar, un cuchillo afilado y una olla grande.
english: I need a cutting board, a sharp knife, and a large pot.

target: Ya habían cerrado cuando llegamos.
english: They had already closed when we arrived.
grammar: Past perfect: "Cuando llegamos, ya había empezado." The pluperfect shows one past action was already done before another.

target: He comido demasiado, no puedo más.
english: I've eaten too much, I can't take any more.
grammar: 'He + past participle' = present perfect. In Spain, it's used for recent past: 'he comido hoy.'

target: Agua que no has de beber, déjala correr.
english: If you can't drink it, let it flow.

target: La realidad es peor de lo que imaginaba.
english: Reality is worse than what I imagined.

target: Ella está muy enfadada conmigo por lo que pasó.
english: She is very angry with me about what happened.

target: La profesora pidió que los padres asistieran a la reunión.
english: The teacher asked that the parents attend the meeting.

target: El parque al que llevamos a los niños tiene columpios.
english: The park we take the kids to has swings.

target: El país del que vengo tiene una cultura muy rica.
english: The country I come from has a very rich culture.

target: No en vano ha sido el departamento con mejores resultados este trimestre.
english: Not for nothing has it been the department with the best results this quarter.

target: Para las seis, habré terminado.
english: By six, I will have finished.
grammar: Future perfect: habré + past participle.

target: He perdido las llaves otra vez.
english: I've lost my keys again.
grammar: Present perfect: he perdido (perder) – haber + past participle.

target: El campeonato mundial de atletismo se celebra cada dos años.
english: The world athletics championship is held every two years.

target: El restaurante es pequeño; no obstante, la comida es excelente.
english: The restaurant is small – nevertheless, the food is excellent.

target: Cabe señalar que esta medida beneficiará a miles de personas.
english: It should be pointed out that this measure will benefit thousands of people.

target: No solo subieron los precios, sino que también redujeron la calidad.
english: Not only did they raise prices, but they also reduced quality.
grammar: No solo... sino que también: correlative connectors.

target: Es fundamental mantener un tono profesional en los correos de trabajo.
english: It is essential to maintain a professional tone in work emails.

target: En la aduana me pidieron que abriera la maleta para una inspección.
english: At customs they asked me to open my suitcase for an inspection.

target: Es como si mi madre tuviera un sexto sentido con los niños.
english: It's as if my mother had a sixth sense with kids.

target: Quienquiera que haya dicho eso, se equivoca.
english: Whoever said that is wrong.
grammar: Quienquiera que + subjunctive = whoever.

target: Si pudiera elegir, viviría cerca del mar.
english: If I could choose, I would live near the sea.

target: Ellos se hablan por teléfono cada noche.
english: They talk to each other on the phone every night.
grammar: Hablarse (reciprocal): se hablan – they talk to each other.

target: El hecho de que no respondiera me preocupó.
english: The fact that he didn't respond worried me.

target: Si pudiera cocinar mejor, invitaría a más gente.
english: If I could cook better, I would invite more people.

target: En el supuesto de que cancelen el vuelo, nos reembolsarán.
english: In the event that they cancel the flight, they will reimburse us.

target: Quienquiera que haya diseñado este itinerario hizo un trabajo increíble.
english: Whoever designed this itinerary did an incredible job.

target: Si hubiera hecho caso a mi padre, no tendría estas deudas.
english: If I had listened to my father, I wouldn't be in debt.

target: Estas camisetas se venden muy bien.
english: These shirts sell very well.
grammar: Passive se: the verb agrees with the grammatical subject. "Se venden camisetas" (camisetas = subject, plural → venden).

target: Se vive bien en esta ciudad.
english: You live well in this city.
grammar: "Se vive" = one lives / people live. Impersonal se with intransitive verbs: "Se vive bien aquí" = People live well here.

target: No solo llegó tarde, sino que además no pidió disculpas.
english: Not only did he arrive late, but he also didn't apologize.

target: Habríamos ganado el contrato si la presentación hubiera sido mejor.
english: We would have won the contract if the presentation had been better.

target: Por un lado quiero ir; por otro lado, estoy muy cansado.
english: On the one hand I want to go – on the other hand, I'm very tired.

target: Mi madre me dijo que mi hermano había llamado mientras estaba fuera.
english: My mother told me my brother had called while I was out.

target: El libro es interesante; sin embargo, el final me decepcionó un poco.
english: The book is interesting – however, the ending disappointed me a little.

target: Acaba de llamar tu madre.
english: Your mother just called.
grammar: `acabar de + infinitive` = 'to have just done X'. `Acabo de comer` = 'I've just eaten'. Despite the English perfect tense, Spanish uses present.

target: Llevo viajando por España tres semanas.
english: I've been traveling around Spain for three weeks.
grammar: "Llevar" + gerund expresses duration: "I've been doing something for X time."

target: Se pusieron a discutir en medio del restaurante.
english: They started arguing in the middle of the restaurant.

target: Se nota a la legua que está enamorado.
english: You can tell from a mile off that he's in love.

target: En cuanto al tema que mencionaste, estoy de acuerdo.
english: Regarding the topic you mentioned, I agree.

target: Por mucho que me cueste admitirlo, ese hotel era un desastre.
english: As much as it pains me to admit it, that hotel was a disaster.

target: Al fin y al cabo, lo importante es que estamos todos bien.
english: At the end of the day, the important thing is that we're all okay.

target: Por mucho que lo intentes, no conseguirás cambiar su forma de pensar.
english: No matter how much you try, you won't manage to change their way of thinking.

target: Sigue lloviendo desde esta mañana.
english: It's been raining since this morning.
grammar: 'Seguir + gerund' = to keep/continue doing. 'Sigue lloviendo' = It keeps raining.

target: Llevo tres años estudiando español.
english: I've been studying Spanish for three years.
grammar: "Llevar" + time + gerund – ongoing duration.

target: No dejo de pensar en lo que me dijiste.
english: I can't stop thinking about what you told me.

target: De haber sabido que vendríais, habría preparado más comida.
english: Had I known you were coming, I would have prepared more food.

target: De hecho, es más complicado de lo que parece.
english: In fact, it's more complicated than it seems.

target: Me resulta difícil concentrarme cuando hay mucho ruido en la oficina.
english: I find it hard to concentrate when there's a lot of noise in the office.

target: La doctora me dijo que el dolor de estómago podría ser estrés.
english: The doctor told me the stomachache could be stress.

target: De haber sabido que era niña, habríamos decorado la habitación de rosa.
english: Had we known it was a girl, we would have decorated the room in pink.

target: No nos avisaron del cambio.
english: They didn't tell us about the change.
grammar: "Nos" = to us (indirect object): "Nos dijo la verdad" = He told us the truth.

target: El camarero preguntó si queríamos postre.
english: The waiter asked if we wanted dessert.
grammar: Reported question with "si": "¿Quieren postre?" → "si queríamos postre."

target: Heredé los ojos azules de mi abuela materna.
english: I inherited my blue eyes from my maternal grandmother.

target: Dejo de responder correos a las seis para desconectar.
english: I stop answering emails at six to disconnect.

target: El cliente nos dijo que no estaba satisfecho con el servicio.
english: The client told us he wasn't satisfied with the service.

target: Me dijo que aquella había sido la mejor decisión de su vida.
english: She told me that had been the best decision of her life.
grammar: 'Esa/esta' becomes 'aquella' in reported speech (distal demonstrative).

target: Por más que busqué, no encontré un vuelo directo a esa isla.
english: No matter how much I searched, I couldn't find a direct flight to that island.

target: El jardín está más bonito que el año pasado.
english: The garden looks nicer than last year.
grammar: `más X que Y` = 'more X than Y', `menos X que Y` = 'less X than Y'. Use `que` (not `de`) before the thing you're comparing to.

target: Puesto que no hay tren directo, tomaremos el autobús.
english: Since there's no direct train, we'll take the bus.

target: El entrenador explicó que debíamos calentar antes de correr.
english: The coach explained that we had to warm up before running.
grammar: Reported speech: "deben" → "debíamos" (present → imperfect) after "explicó que."

target: No es que no me guste viajar, sino que prefiero planificarlo bien.
english: It's not that I don't like traveling, but I prefer to plan it well.

target: De no ser por el apoyo de mi familia, no lo habría conseguido.
english: Were it not for my family's support, I wouldn't have made it.

target: El arrepentimiento me persigue desde que tomé aquella decisión sin pensar en las consecuencias.
english: Regret has haunted me since I made that decision without thinking about the consequences.

target: Huelga decir que su contribución fue fundamental.
english: Needless to say, his contribution was fundamental.
grammar: Huelga decir que = needless to say (very formal register).

target: Mis padres están casados desde hace treinta años.
english: My parents have been married for thirty years.
grammar: "ser" for personality traits and inherent qualities. "Están cariñosos" would mean they're being affectionate right now (unusual behavior).

target: Dejamos de vernos cuando ella se mudó al extranjero.
english: We stopped seeing each other when she moved abroad.

target: De no haber sido por el plazo, habríamos hecho un mejor trabajo.
english: If it hadn't been for the deadline, we would have done a better job.

target: Me arrepentí de no haber dicho lo que sentía cuando tuve la oportunidad.
english: I regretted not saying what I felt when I had the chance.

target: La verdadera riqueza no se mide en dinero, sino en experiencias y relaciones.
english: True wealth is not measured in money, but in experiences and relationships.

target: Los fines de semana me levanto tarde.
english: On weekends I get up late.
grammar: "Los fines de semana" – using "los" with a time expression means "every" or "on." Los lunes = on Mondays. Without "los" it's a specific one.

target: Huelga decir que la puntualidad es fundamental.
english: It goes without saying that punctuality is essential.
grammar: Huelga decir que = it goes without saying that (very formal).

target: De no ser por el mapa, nos habríamos perdido completamente.
english: If it weren't for the map, we would have gotten completely lost.

target: Eso es harina de otro costal; no tiene nada que ver.
english: That's a different kettle of fish (lit. that's flour from another sack) – it has nothing to do with it.
grammar: When a negative word comes after the verb, `no` goes before it. `No vi a nadie`, `nunca lo hago`. Two negatives don't cancel – they reinforce.

target: Dicho esto, el viaje superó con creces mis expectativas.
english: That said, the trip far exceeded my expectations.

target: Terminada la reunión, todos se dirigieron a la salida.
english: Once the meeting was over, everyone headed for the exit.
grammar: Absolute participial clause: participle + noun = 'once X was done'.

target: Cada vez más personas se informan a través de internet.
english: More and more people get their information through the internet.
grammar: "resultar" (like gustar). "Expresarse" = to express oneself (reflexive). "En otro idioma" = in another language.

target: Me pilló por sorpresa; no me lo esperaba para nada.
english: It caught me by surprise (lit. it caught/grabbed me) – i didn't expect it at all.

target: La nómina de este mes incluye las horas extra que hice en febrero.
english: This month's paycheck includes the overtime I did in February.

target: La crianza de los hijos es el mayor reto y la mayor recompensa.
english: Raising children is the greatest challenge and the greatest reward.

target: Es lamentable que no se valore lo suficiente el trabajo de los profesores.
english: It is regrettable that the work of teachers is not valued enough.

target: Cuanto más viajo, más me doy cuenta de lo grande que es el mundo.
english: The more I travel, the more I realize how big the world is.

target: Hice una lista de la compra para no olvidarme de nada en el supermercado.
english: I made a shopping list so I wouldn't forget anything at the supermarket.

target: Cuanto más practico, mejor me siento con el idioma.
english: The more I practice, the better I feel with the language.
grammar: Cuanto más...mejor = the more...the better, comparative correlation.

target: Le diagnosticaron diabetes y ahora tiene que controlar el azúcar.
english: They diagnosed him with diabetes and now he has to monitor his sugar.

target: No es sino trabajando todos juntos como lograremos superar esta crisis.
english: It is only by working together that we will overcome this crisis.
grammar: No es sino + gerund + como = it is only by... that (emphatic cleft).

target: Después de la mudanza tardamos una semana entera en deshacer todas las cajas.
english: After the move it took us a whole week to unpack all the boxes.

target: En la carta hay platos sin gluten y sin lactosa para personas con intolerancias.
english: The menu has gluten-free and lactose-free dishes for people with intolerances.

target: Lo realmente preocupante no es el problema en sí, sino la falta de respuesta.
english: What is truly worrying is not the problem itself, but the lack of response.

target: Pasamos el control de seguridad del aeropuerto sin problemas.
english: We passed through airport security without any problems.

target: No me llamó; es más, ni siquiera me mandó un mensaje.
english: He didn't call me – what's more, he didn't even send me a message.
grammar: "Es más" = what's more / moreover. Escalates or adds to a previous point.

target: Mi sobrina me dibujó un retrato y me lo regaló por mi cumpleaños.
english: My niece drew a portrait of me and gave it to me for my birthday.

target: Habiendo recorrido toda la costa, puedo decir que el sur es lo mejor.
english: Having traveled the whole coast, I can say the south is the best.

target: A diferencia de otros turistas, preferimos la comida local.
english: Unlike other tourists, we prefer local food.

target: No solo habla español, sino que también domina el francés.
english: Not only does he speak Spanish, but he also masters French.
grammar: No solo...sino que también = not only...but also.

target: Hago pesas y abdominales tres días a la semana en el gimnasio.
english: I do weights and sit-ups three days a week at the gym.

target: Las cataratas del Iguazú están en la frontera entre Argentina y Brasil.
english: Iguazu Falls are on the border between Argentina and Brazil.

target: Si mi hermana hubiera venido, la fiesta habría sido mejor.
english: If my sister had come, the party would have been better.

target: Sea cual sea el destino, lo importante es disfrutar del camino.
english: Whatever the destination, the important thing is to enjoy the journey.

target: Lo cierto es que viajar en temporada baja tiene muchas ventajas.
english: The truth is that traveling in the off-season has many advantages.

target: Perdimos la conexión del vuelo por un retraso en la escala.
english: We missed the connecting flight because of a delay at the layover.

target: Si el proyecto hubiera ido bien, me habrían dado una promoción.
english: If the project had gone well, they would have given me a promotion.

target: Si alguna vez tienes la oportunidad, no te lo pienses dos veces.
english: If you ever have the opportunity, don't think twice.

target: Habría sido mejor si nos hubiéramos quedado en casa.
english: It would have been better if we had stayed home.

target: A menos que encontremos financiación, el proyecto se cancelará.
english: Unless we find funding, the project will be cancelled.

target: Habría aceptado la oferta si las condiciones hubieran sido mejores.
english: I would have accepted the offer if the conditions had been better.

target: Habría aceptado el trabajo si me hubieran ofrecido mejor sueldo.
english: I would have accepted the job if they had offered me a better salary.

target: Aunque hubiera tenido más tiempo, el resultado habría sido el mismo.
english: Even if I had had more time, the result would have been the same.
